newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Proer bank plan is cost effective - gov't.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Proer bank plan is cost effective - gov't.

text.p: Brazil's program to encourage bank mergers and acquisitions, known as Proer, has so far cost the government about 292 million reais, making it a cost effective program, Economic Policy Secretary Jose Mendonca de Barros told Gazeta Mercantil.
The cost is "much less than what it would cost to resolve a crisis in the financial sector," which may have resulted without the plan, Mendonca de Barros wrote in a report for the newspaper.

The official said the Central Bank had made some 13.158 billion reais in credit available to banks between November 1995 and June 1996, which has cost the government about 292 million reais in financing charges.
The program was designed to encourage healthy banks to buy up weak financial institutions and merge with each other.
